tasks.title: Character classes
tasks.statement: Write classify(s: &str) -> (usize, usize, usize, usize): the number of letters, digits, whitespace and other characters (by Unicode rules: is_alphabetic, is_numeric, is_whitespace).
tasks.hint: Four counters and an if / else if chain.

tasks.title: Digits in different bases
tasks.statement: Write hex_sum(s: &str) -> u32: the sum of the values of the hexadecimal digits in the string (to_digit(16)); non-hex characters are skipped.
tasks.hint: filter_map(|c| c.to_digit(16))

tasks.title: A number to a string in any base
tasks.statement: Write to_radix(n: u32, radix: u32) -> String: the representation of n in base radix (2…36) with lowercase letters; for 0 — «0». Use char::from_digit.
tasks.hint: The remainders of division are the digits in reverse order.

tasks.title: Split on several separators
tasks.statement: Write tokens(s: &str) -> Vec<String>: words separated by any of the characters «,», «;», «:» or whitespace; empty pieces are skipped.
tasks.hint: split accepts a closure as a pattern.

tasks.title: splitn
tasks.statement: Write parse_cmd(line: &str) -> (String, String): the command and the rest of the line. Split at the first space (splitn(2, ' ')); if there is no space, the second part is empty. Do not trim the rest.
tasks.hint: splitn(2, ' ') does not split the remainder.

tasks.title: strip_prefix
tasks.statement: Write command(line: &str) -> String: «ECHO <text>» → the text; «UP <text>» → the text in uppercase; otherwise «неизвестная команда». Use strip_prefix.
tasks.hint: strip_prefix returns Option<&str>.

tasks.title: Sentences
tasks.statement: Write sentences(s: &str) -> Vec<String>: split the text into sentences, keeping the end mark (. ! ?) at the end of each, and trim the spaces at the edges. split_inclusive with a closure.
tasks.hint: split_inclusive keeps the separator in the piece.

tasks.title: Strip the wrapping
tasks.statement: Write unquote(s: &str) -> String: remove from both ends any quotes «"» and «'» and spaces (trim_matches with a closure).
tasks.hint: trim_matches(|c| …) trims from both ends.

tasks.title: Positions of occurrences
tasks.statement: Write positions(text: &str, pat: &str) -> Vec<usize>: the byte positions of all (non-overlapping) occurrences of pat (match_indices); pat is not empty.
tasks.hint: match_indices returns (position, match).

tasks.title: File extension
tasks.statement: Write extension(name: &str) -> Option<&str>: the extension after the last dot; None if there is no dot, if the dot is at the start (a hidden file «.bashrc») or at the end.
tasks.hint: rfind('.') and a slice after the dot.

tasks.title: In-place edits
tasks.statement: Write censor(s: &mut String, bad: &str): replace the first occurrence of bad with asterisks of the same length in characters (replace_range) — if bad is absent, change nothing.
tasks.hint: find gives a byte index; the range is i..i + bad.len().

tasks.title: Keep only letters
tasks.statement: Write letters_only(s: &mut String): keep only letters in the string (retain + is_alphabetic).
tasks.hint: s.retain(|c| c.is_alphabetic())

tasks.title: Truncate by characters
tasks.statement: Write truncate_chars(s: &str, n: usize) -> String: the first n characters; if the string is longer, append «…» at the end (characters, not bytes; do not cut in the middle of a character).
tasks.hint: chars().take(n).collect::<String>()

tasks.title: Table
tasks.statement: Write table(rows: &[(&str, f64)]) -> Vec<String>: lines of the form «<name, width of the longest> | <number right-aligned in a field of 8 with two decimals>»; the name is left-aligned.

tasks.title: Number bases with format
tasks.statement: Write formats(n: u32) -> Vec<String>: n in decimal, hexadecimal (with the 0x prefix, 4 digits zero-padded), binary (8 digits zero-padded) and octal: for 255 → ["255", "0x00ff", "11111111", "377"].

tasks.title: Sign and precision
tasks.statement: Write signed(x: f64) -> String: the number with an explicit sign and two digits after the decimal point, centered in a field of 9 characters with the fill «.»: signed(3.14159) = «..+3.14..».
tasks.hint: {:.^+9.2} — fill «.», center, sign, width 9, precision 2.

tasks.title: Width from an argument
tasks.statement: Write pad_left(s: &str, width: usize, fill: char) -> String: right-align s to a width of width characters, adding the fill character on the left (the format does not take the fill from a variable — add it by hand). If s is not shorter than width, return it as is.
tasks.hint: The number of fill characters is width - n.

tasks.title: Display for money
tasks.statement: The struct Money(i64) stores kopecks. Implement Display: «123.05 ₽» for 12305, «-0.99 ₽» for −99, «0.00 ₽» for 0.
tasks.hint: The sign separately, rubles a / 100, kopecks {:02}.

tasks.title: Display that respects the width
tasks.statement: The struct Name(String) implements Display through f.pad(&self.0), so that width and alignment work: «[{:>8}]» for Name("Аня") gives «[     Аня]».
tasks.hint: f.pad takes the width, alignment and precision (truncation) into account.

tasks.title: Debug by hand
tasks.statement: The struct User { name: String, age: u32, secret: String } — implement Debug by hand via debug_struct so that the field secret is not printed (the output is «User { name: "Аня", age: 30 }»).
tasks.hint: debug_struct("User").field(…).finish()

tasks.title: Display for a matrix
tasks.statement: The struct Matrix(Vec<Vec<i32>>) implements Display: rows separated by a newline (no empty line at the end), numbers in a row separated by a space, each right-aligned in a field of width 3: «  1  2», «  3  4».
tasks.hint: writeln!(f)? between rows, write!(f, "{:>3}", x)? for the numbers.

tasks.title: Parsing «key=value»
tasks.statement: Write parse_kv(line: &str) -> Option<(String, i32)>: «name = 42» → ("name", 42); None if there is no «=», the key is empty, or the value is not an integer.
tasks.hint: split_once, trim, parse().ok()?

tasks.title: A CSV line to numbers
tasks.statement: Write parse_row(s: &str) -> Result<Vec<f64>, String>: comma-separated numbers (with spaces around); on error — Err(«плохое поле: <field>»).
tasks.hint: collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()

tasks.title: A number with a prefix
tasks.statement: Write parse_num(s: &str) -> Option<i64>: decimal, or with the prefix 0x (hex), 0b (binary) or 0o (octal); the sign «-» is allowed before the prefix. Underscores are ignored.
tasks.hint: First remove the sign and underscores, then check the prefixes.

tasks.title: Frequency report
tasks.statement: Write report(text: &str) -> Vec<String>: words in lowercase and their frequencies; lines of the form «word: N», in descending order of N, ties broken alphabetically.
tasks.hint: Counters in a Vec of pairs, then sort_by.

tasks.title: Centering
tasks.statement: Write center_lines(text: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String>: center each line of the text (lines) in a field of width width (with the format {:^w$}); lines longer than width are left unchanged.
tasks.hint: format!("{:^w$}", l, w = width)

tasks.title: snake_case to CamelCase
tasks.statement: Write to_camel(s: &str) -> String: «my_var_name» → «MyVarName» (the separator is «_»; empty pieces are skipped).
tasks.hint: The first letter of each piece goes to uppercase.

tasks.title: CamelCase to snake_case
tasks.statement: Write to_snake(s: &str) -> String: «MyVarName» → «my_var_name» (a «_» is put before each capital letter except the first character).
tasks.hint: out.extend(c.to_lowercase()) — to_lowercase returns an iterator.

tasks.title: Vigenère cipher
tasks.statement: Write vigenere(text: &str, key: &str) -> String: the Vigenère cipher for Latin lowercase letters (a–z); the key is lowercase letters, not empty; the key advances only on letters of the text; other characters stay unchanged.
tasks.hint: The key position j increases only on a Latin letter.

tasks.title: Bytes of characters
tasks.statement: Write byte_lens(s: &str) -> Vec<(char, usize)>: each character and how many bytes it takes in UTF-8 (len_utf8).
tasks.hint: c.len_utf8() — 1…4.
